text: Acts as a drop-in replacement for Terraform, keeping existing workflows and configs
quote: It serves as a drop-in replacement for Terraform, preserving your existing workflows and configurations.

text: `tofu plan` generates an execution plan showing proposed infrastructure changes before applying
quote: The `tofu plan` command creates an execution plan, which lets you preview the changes that OpenTofu plans to make to your infrastructure.

text: Speculative plans let developers verify change effects before submitting for code review
quote: developers can use speculative plans to verify the effect of their changes before submitting them for code review

text: Destroy mode creates a plan to tear down all managed remote objects, leaving an empty state
quote: Destroy mode: creates a plan whose goal is to destroy all remote objects that currently exist, leaving an empty OpenTofu state.

text: Refresh-only mode updates state/output values to match real-world changes made outside OpenTofu
quote: Refresh-only mode: creates a plan whose goal is only to update the OpenTofu state and any root module output values to match changes made to remote objects outside of OpenTofu.

text: `tofu test` runs configuration tests against real infrastructure, checking assertions then tearing it down
quote: The `tofu test` command lets you test your OpenTofu configuration by creating real infrastructure and checking that the required conditions (assertions) are met. Once the test is complete, OpenTofu destroys the resources it created.

text: `tofu import` brings existing resources under OpenTofu management
quote: The `tofu import` command imports existing resources into OpenTofu.

text: Supports encrypting state and plan files at rest, locally and in remote backends, using AES-GCM
quote: OpenTofu supports encrypting state and plan files at rest, both for local storage and when using a backend.

text: Encryption also extends to data read via the terraform_remote_state data source
quote: OpenTofu supports encrypting state and plan files at rest, both for local storage and when using a backend. In addition, you can also use encryption with the `terraform_remote_state` data source.

text: -exclude flag lets you selectively skip resources during plan/apply operations
quote: Selectively exclude resources from operations with the -exclude flag. This provides more control during testing and rollouts, allowing you to focus on specific parts of your infrastructure.

text: Dynamically generate provider configurations with for_each for multi-region/multi-environment setups
quote: Dynamically generate provider configurations with for_each, eliminating repetitive code and improving maintainability. Perfect for multi-region deployments, multi-environment setups (dev/staging/prod)...

text: Centralized module version variables let you update all modules programmatically in one change
quote: Update all your modules programmatically with a single variable change. Never miss updating a module version by accident - keep your infrastructure consistent and secure with centralized version management.

text: Builds a dependency graph and parallelizes creation/modification of non-dependent resources
quote: OpenTofu builds a graph of all your resources, and parallelizes the creation and modification of any non-dependent resources.

text: Ecosystem of 3,900+ providers and 23,600+ modules for managing infrastructure across clouds
quote: With a thriving ecosystem of 3,900+ providers and 23,600+ modules, you can build and manage infrastructure across every cloud platform with confidence.

text: -out=FILE saves a generated plan to disk, which can later be applied via `tofu apply`
quote: You can use the optional `-out=FILE` option to save the generated plan to a file on disk, which you can later execute by passing the file to `tofu apply` as an extra argument.

text: .tofu files take precedence over .tf files, letting modules support both OpenTofu and Terraform
quote: This ensures that `.tofu` files always take precedence over `.tf` files when both are available. This scenario can be useful for module authors who want their modules to support both OpenTofu and Terraform.

text: Backwards-compatible so existing code continues to work across versions
quote: Backwards-compatible - so that the existing code can drive value for years to come

text: As part of the Linux Foundation, OpenTofu guarantees it will remain truly open source
quote: Now that we are part of the Linux Foundation, we can guarantee that OpenTofu will remain: Truly open source
